body.statement: For every \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0\le r<1\), the map \(x\mapsto q_{\beta}(r,x)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R\). Moreover, for every \(c_0,c_1\in\mathbb R\) and \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) holds if and only if \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\).
body.justification: Convexity supplies the global single-crossing fact needed to optimize over arbitrary compact alternatives.
body.gap: Shenfeld and van Handel prove Gaussian-measure convexity and equality cases but do not derive convexity of conditional selected-score quantiles.
body.consumer: Power calculations need only the least clinically relevant effect coordinate, even when the prespecified alternative set is nonconvex.
